title: Linear Relational Decoding of Morphological Relations in Language Models

contributions.purpose: Determine whether and how morphological derivations (pluralization, tense, nominalization, resultatives) are encoded in transformer LM latent representations.
contributions.mechanism: Show that a purely linear (multiplicative) approximation F(s)=Ws, where s is a mid-layer base-form representation and W is a local model Jacobian derivative, is necessary and sufficient to approximate morphological derivations, dropping the bias/scaling of the affine LRE of Hernandez et al. (2023).
contributions.evaluation: Achieves above 80% faithfulness across most morphological tasks in the Bigger Analogy Test Set; holds across different language models and across eight languages spanning typological categories.
contributions.source_quote: We show that the truly linear approximation Ws, where s is a middle layer representation of the base form and W is a local model derivative, is necessary and sufficient to approximate morphological derivations.

contributions.purpose: Clarify when additive vs. multiplicative (affine vs. linear) mechanisms govern relational approximation in model latents.
contributions.mechanism: Comparative analysis applying affine LRE and the linear multiplicative operator across morphological vs. encyclopedic/semantic relations, adapting analogical datasets (Bigger Analogy Test Set) to relational contexts.
contributions.evaluation: Qualitative/quantitative finding: encyclopedic and semantic relations benefit from the affine LRE bias term, but morphological relations do not; linear approximation for morphological forms reaches near-equivalent faithfulness to the affine LRE.
contributions.source_quote: we find that relative to linear approximation, encyclopedic and semantic relations benefit from the affine LRE, but not morphological relations.

self_declared_provenance.quote: we create an approximator which maps base representations ('compute') s to its corresponding output representations ('computable'), as F(s)=Ws similar to the LRE seen in Hernandez et al. (2023) but omitting the bias term b_r and hyperparameter beta.

Our study reproduces and extends existing research. Specifically, we apply the affine Linear Relational Embedding (LRE) method to novel relational categories encompassing a diverse range of domains, including derivational and inflectional morphology, encyclopedic knowledge, and lexical semantics.
We find that the original linear relational embedding developed by Paccanaro and Hinton (2001), a multiplicative operator, is effective within specific relations.

notes: Nuanced/comparative result: linear (no-bias) approximation matches affine LRE for morphology but affine is better for encyclopedic/semantic relations, i.e., no single mechanism wins everywhere. Paper is ICLR 2025 reject. Contributions are analysis/findings rather than a new method.
